claims.statement: The Investment Policy Committee owns strategic multi-asset weights and binding band decisions; portfolio-manager activity outside a stated tolerance band requires approval, while the mandate-specific band governs when it is tighter.

The committee strategic allocation for a global balanced mandate is 45% global equities, 35% global fixed income, 10% real assets, and 10% private markets for eligible clients; for an ineligible client, the private-markets allocation is reallocated pro rata across liquid sleeves.

The ordinary tolerance bands are plus or minus 5 percentage points for equities and fixed income and plus or minus 3 percentage points for real assets; private markets does not have an ordinary tradable tolerance band.

The committee underwrites duration diversification at a reduced level because the rates research finds stock-bond correlation unstable and not reliably negative; its March 2026 adoption is the basis for a 5-point rather than prior 7-point equity band.

The rates-regime note recommends reviewing the bands rather than setting them itself, and the committee will review strategic weights against its working assumption at the 2026 annual review without having changed the strategic weights for it yet.

When research cited by a mandate guide is superseded or withdrawn, its derived weight or band is suspended and escalated to the committee; managers must record the note, replacement if any, dependent weights, and affected accounts, and may neither carry forward the old control nor adopt the replacement directly.

Private-markets exposure is managed through commitment pacing rather than rebalancing: denominator-effect drift above strategic weight is not traded as a breach, while drift caused by over-commitment is a pacing failure requiring escalation.

A private-markets commitment requires an eligibility determination before approval, and eligibility is a regulatory constraint outside portfolio-manager discretion; eligibility alone is insufficient because suitability and the private-markets liquidity constraint still apply.

The binding private-markets liquidity limit is that unfunded commitments may not exceed two years of liquid portfolio spending and must be underwritten against client spending requirements rather than expected return.

The guidance is reviewed annually and out of cycle whenever a cited research note is reissued or withdrawn; cleared escalations require a recorded condition, authority, facts, and date, or are treated as unapproved in audit.

This binding internal guidance governs the US taxable fixed-income sleeve for US taxable client accounts—US Treasuries, agency MBS, investment-grade corporates, and municipal credit—while non-US sovereign and emerging-market debt remain governed by the multi-asset sleeve guidance.

For top federal marginal-bracket clients, municipal credit has a 22% target against an 18% neutral weight, while clients below the top bracket remain at the 18% neutral municipal weight without the private-activity concentration.

Investment-grade corporate credit has a 28% target against a 32% neutral weight; its four-percentage-point underweight funds the municipal overweight, and suspension of the municipal overweight returns both municipal and corporate positions to neutral.

The municipal overweight is an after-tax, top-bracket position rather than a credit-only position: the supporting research says private-activity paper's advantage appears only after tax and the fundamental case alone supports only neutral to modest overweight.

Within the municipal allocation, no more than 35% may be in any one preferred sector; positions in standalone senior living, single-asset student housing, or single-obligor industrial-development paper require approval; municipal duration is restricted to 8–15 years and extensions cannot be granted portfolio-wide.

A tax-loss-harvest replacement in the municipal allocation must satisfy the municipal sector limit at settlement, so a replacement that concentrates a preferred sector above the limit is a breach on settlement.

Each target weight has a ±2-percentage-point market-value tolerance measured at month end; ordinary drift outside the band is rebalanced in the next monthly cycle and requires approval under the discretion matrix.

A cited research note's supersession or withdrawal suspends the weights derived from it rather than triggering automatic rebalancing or manager-led recalculation; the manager must escalate the superseded note, any replacement, dependent weights, and affected accounts to the Committee, which alone can re-adopt a binding control.

The guidance is reviewed quarterly and out of cycle when a cited research note is reissued or withdrawn, and a cleared escalation requires a record of the condition, authority, facts relied on, and date or it is treated as unapproved in audit.

The guidance constrains implementation of Municipal Credit 2025-06 and IG Spreads 2025-09 by converting their municipal increase and corporate funding recommendations into fixed, client-scoped binding weights; research does not authorize a portfolio manager to choose a replacement control.
The investment-grade corporate underweight is valuation-driven rather than a credit-deterioration call, and it is carry-negative if spreads remain range-bound.

Portfolio managers have base discretion; senior portfolio managers have expanded discretion and may clear one escalation condition per account; Committee approval is required for matters beyond senior discretion, accounts with more than one escalation condition, and exceptions to stated bands. Mandate-specific guides may tighten but not broaden this authority.

Single-issuer positions up to 3% of account market value are within portfolio-manager discretion, positions up to 5% are within senior portfolio-manager discretion, and positions above 5% require Committee approval plus a written concentration rationale; such positions are also subject to the concentrated-position guide.

Regardless of size, approval is required for an ordinary out-of-band weight, a position barred by a binding underweight sector limit, a concentrated-position hedge, municipal duration beyond the applicable band, and every private-markets commitment.

When a cited research note is superseded or withdrawn, the manager must suspend the dependent weight, escalate to the Committee rather than re-derive it, and may neither carry the prior weight forward nor directly adopt a replacement recommendation; the escalation records the old note, replacement if any, dependent weights, and affected accounts.

A research-change suspension is distinct from ordinary drift: the global multi-asset guide prescribes a return to the prior Committee-adopted level pending review, while a US taxable fixed-income suspension is not automatically rebalanced because the successor weight is a Committee decision.

Approval cannot clear discretionary trading of employer securities during a blackout period, a private-markets commitment for a client ineligible under the eligibility guide, or a breach of a stated regulatory requirement.

Private-markets eligibility must be determined and documented before the strategy is offered, remains separate from suitability and liquidity, and a determination made before the effective date cannot support a new investment made on or after that date.

The private-markets liquidity constraint is binding in the global multi-asset guide: underwrite unfunded commitments against the client's spending requirement and do not allow them to exceed two years of liquid-portfolio spending.

A cleared escalation must record the condition, clearing authority, facts relied on, and date; without a recorded basis it is treated as an unapproved position in audit and charged back to the clearing manager's file review.

Concentration and private-markets matters carry separate audit records: concentrated positions require a documented suitability determination at acquisition and annual review, while private-markets eligibility records the pathway, evidence, determiner, and date and is treated as absent in audit if that basis is missing.

Private-markets exposure is managed through commitment pacing rather than ordinary rebalancing: a denominator-effect increase above the strategic weight is not traded, while an increase caused by over-commitment is a pacing failure that must be escalated.
A single-security position is concentrated when it exceeds 15% of the client’s liquid portfolio market value, or exceeds 10% when the security is the client’s employer or an affiliate.

A concentrated position requires a documented suitability determination at acquisition and each annual review that records the client’s stated reason for holding, tax cost of unwinding, and any restriction preventing an unwind; a holding preference alone is insufficient, and the file must record explained concentration risk and an informed client decision.
Every concentrated position requires a written unwind plan reviewed annually, and an unchanged plan for three consecutive reviews is evidence it is not being applied and must be escalated under D.4.
Hedging a concentrated position requires approval under D.3 regardless of size, and tax consequences of collars, prepaid forwards, and exchange funds must be addressed in writing before execution.
For employer securities, the file must record applicable trading windows, blackout periods, pre-clearance requirements, and any Rule 10b5-1 plan in force.
Employer securities may not be traded on the firm’s discretion during a blackout period; this prohibition may not be cleared by approval.

The discretion matrix separately requires Committee approval and a written concentration rationale for a single-issuer position above 5% of account market value, after which it is subject to the concentrated-position guide; audit documentation for a cleared escalation does not replace this guide’s separate concentration records.

Firm guidance requires a documented eligibility determination before any private-markets strategy is offered; eligibility is a regulatory determination outside portfolio-manager discretion, and a private-markets commitment for an ineligible client cannot be cleared by approval.

Effective 2026-06-29, SEC Order IA-7104 adjusts Rule 205-3's qualified-client tests to at least $1.4 million of adviser-managed assets immediately after contract entry or net worth greater than $2.7 million immediately before contract entry; the firm's eligibility guide implements Order Q.2 rather than replacing it with an independently operative restatement.

A qualified-client determination made before 2026-06-29 remains valid for the pre-effective-date advisory contract or private-fund investment and does not require divestment, but it cannot support a contract, investment, or new subscription on or after that date; the carried-forward file must identify that prior thresholds were used.

Order IA-7104 adjusts only Rule 205-3 qualified-client dollar tests, leaving Regulation D accredited-investor criteria and the Investment Company Act qualified-purchaser definition unchanged; accredited-investor status is determined separately, and eligibility must be checked against the status required by the strategy or offering.

Each eligibility determination records the pathway, evidence, determining person, and date; the adviser must retain its basis, including the dollar test relied on and determination date, and audit treats a determination without a recorded basis as no determination.

Eligibility is necessary but insufficient for a private-markets commitment: firm guidance separately requires suitability and compliance with the private-markets liquidity constraint, under which unfunded commitments may not exceed two years of liquid-portfolio spending and must be underwritten against spending needs.

MA-GL-PRIVATE-MARKETS 2025-12 is a research view applicable to positions taken on or after 2026-01-01 that supports a 10–20% strategic allocation for eligible clients with a genuine ten-year horizon, favors secondaries and private credit, underweights primary buyout, and treats eligibility as a regulatory rather than research matter.

For global balanced mandates, the firm assigns a 10% private-markets strategic sleeve only to eligible clients and reallocates it pro rata across liquid sleeves for ineligible clients; private-markets exposure is managed by commitment pacing, with denominator-effect drift not traded and over-commitment drift escalated.

For the Rule 205-3 net-worth route, the order excludes a primary residence's value and residence-secured indebtedness up to fair market value, while allowing a natural person to include assets jointly held with a spouse.

A private-markets commitment requires approval after the documented eligibility gate, but approval cannot clear an ineligible client or another regulatory breach; a cleared approval record must identify the condition, authority level, specific facts, and date, or audit treats the position as unapproved.
Frozen research editions are never edited in place: an earlier edition remains the basis of record for positions taken while it stood, even after a later edition is published.

EQ-US-SEMI-CAPEX 2026-02 supersedes the 2025-06 edition for positions taken on or after 2026-03-01 and sets the semiconductor capital-equipment view to neutral, while the superseded 2025-06 edition remains the basis of record for positions taken while it stood.

EQ-GL-AI-INFRA-POWER 2026-01 P.4 modifies EQ-US-SEMI-CAPEX 2026-02 S.4 by treating grid interconnection as a cap on the rate of capacity addition rather than eventual demand, not as authorization for a different semiconductor weight.

The taxable fixed-income guide binds a 22% municipal target for top-bracket accounts against an 18% neutral weight; its four-point overweight and private-activity concentration are adopted from FI-US-MUNI-CREDIT 2025-06 M.1 and rest on M.2, while below-top-bracket accounts remain at the 18% neutral weight without that concentration.

FI-US-MUNI-CREDIT 2025-06 states that its private-activity municipal overweight depends on top-bracket holders largely being outside AMT; a phase-out reduction that draws materially more such holders into AMT means the M.1 recommendation does not survive, while fundamentals alone support only neutral to modest overweight.

IRS Revenue Procedure 2025-41 N.3 supersedes FI-US-MUNI-CREDIT 2025-06 M.2 as to the after-tax premise for affected taxpayers in taxable years beginning on or after 2026-01-01: it changes the AMT phase-out thresholds on which M.2 relied, while specified private-activity-bond interest remains an AMT preference.
IRS Revenue Procedure 2025-41 N.5 preserves FI-US-MUNI-CREDIT 2025-06 M.5's qualified-501(c)(3) bond treatment: interest on those bonds is not an AMT preference and is unaffected by the procedure.

When a cited research note is superseded or withdrawn, the taxable fixed-income guide suspends the derived weight rather than carrying it forward until the Committee re-adopts it against a replacement; a suspension-driven band condition is not automatically rebalanced.

Suspending the municipal overweight also suspends its paired four-point investment-grade corporate underweight and returns both to neutral because the corporate underweight funds the municipal allocation.

On a superseded or withdrawn cited note, the escalation must identify the prior note, replacement if any, derived weights, and affected accounts; a manager may neither carry forward the old weight nor adopt replacement research as a binding weight, because that adoption is a Committee act.
A cleared escalation must record its condition, clearing authority, facts relied on, and date; without a recorded basis it is treated as an unapproved position in audit.
No approval may clear a position that breaches a stated regulatory requirement because regulatory requirements are not investment discretion.

FI-US-MUNI-CREDIT 2025-06 applies to positions taken on or after 2025-07-01 and remains the available municipal research edition; its M.8 requires immediate review and re-issue when the M.2 tax treatment changes.

The taxable fixed-income guide makes automatic suspension contingent on a cited research note being superseded or withdrawn; because the available municipal note has neither marker, the evidence does not establish an automatic suspension, return to neutral, or successor municipal target solely from Revenue Procedure 2025-41's effect on M.2.

Research views, binding firm guidance, regulatory overlays, and position assembly have distinct authority: research records a desk conclusion and assumptions, guidance supplies binding controls, an overlay constrains implementation, and the applicable frozen edition remains the basis of record for positions taken while it stood.

For a research-dependent control whose cited note is superseded or withdrawn, the required response is to suspend and escalate rather than carry the control forward, re-derive it, automatically rebalance it, or directly adopt replacement research; Committee adoption creates any successor binding control.

Private-markets eligibility is a documented pre-offer regulatory gate separate from suitability, liquidity, and commitment approval; a determination made before SEC Order IA-7104's effective date cannot support a new contract or private-fund investment on or after 2026-06-29.

IRS Revenue Procedure 2025-41 N.3 supersedes the municipal note's threshold-dependent after-tax premise for affected taxpayers in taxable years beginning on or after 2026-01-01, while N.5 preserves qualified-501(c)(3) bond treatment; the procedure does not select a replacement municipal allocation.

The September 2026 FOMC statement is effective on publication, and it raises the federal-funds target range by 25 basis points to 3-3/4 to 4 percent, judging a somewhat more restrictive stance appropriate in support of the dual mandate.
The FOMC's stated rationale is that inflation remains elevated relative to its 2 percent objective and that the September action supports a timelier return to that objective.

The September statement separately continues Treasury and agency mortgage-backed-security holdings reductions at the previously announced pace while maintaining ample reserves, with no announced pace change.

For any additional target-range adjustments, the FOMC will consider cumulative policy effects, policy lags, and economic and financial developments; the statement expressly describes no future path or committed sequence, and says the Committee will assess data and outlook at each meeting and adjust as appropriate if risks could impede its goals.

The October duration note applies to positions taken on or after 2026-11-01 and treats the September communication as a decision rather than a path; its central case assumes one further increase over twelve months versus one and a half market-implied increases, with that half-step gap the entire basis for a modest, non-conviction duration recommendation.

The duration desk recommends +0.4 years versus benchmark in the five-to-ten-year sector, excludes the long end, and expresses an expected 2s10s steepening through a steepening bias rather than a parallel duration extension.

The desk's long-end exclusion reflects its view that term premium is fair to cheap, long-end supply remains heavy, and there is no catalyst for compression within twelve months; its stated risks include a sequence of inflation prints, higher long-end supply after a fiscal event, and disorderly term-premium repricing.

Revenue Procedure 2025-41 applies to taxable years beginning “on or after” 2026-01-01: its AMT exemption is $90,100 for an unmarried individual and $140,200 for married joint filers or surviving spouses, its phase-out thresholds are $500,000 and $1,000,000 respectively, and those thresholds are not indexed before taxable years beginning 2030-01-01.

For a specified private activity bond—defined for this purpose as a section 141 private activity bond issued after 1986-08-07 with section 103 tax-exempt interest—interest remains an “item of tax preference” included in alternative minimum taxable income, and Revenue Procedure 2025-41 does not modify that definition or treatment.

Revenue Procedure 2025-41 explicitly preserves the qualified-501(c)(3) exception: interest on a qualified section 145 bond is not an AMT preference or part of alternative minimum taxable income, while the municipal research says nonprofit hospitals and private higher education are predominantly qualified 501(c)(3) bonds and airport special-facility paper predominantly is not.

Municipal Credit 2025-06 makes its private-activity recommendation contingent on AMT phase-out thresholds not drawing materially more top-bracket holders into AMT; Revenue Procedure 2025-41’s 2026 threshold reset is therefore an overlay on that after-tax premise for affected taxpayers and non-excepted instruments, not a replacement municipal recommendation.

Municipal Credit 2025-06 states that credit fundamentals and constrained supply are independent of its AMT-dependent after-tax case, but support only a neutral-to-modest overweight rather than the full M.1 overweight.

Municipal Credit 2025-06 requires immediate review and re-issue for an announced change to the M.2 tax treatment, while the allocation guide adopts its 22% top-bracket municipal target, four-point overweight, and private-activity concentration from M.1/M.2 rather than allowing a portfolio manager to select a replacement target.

When the guide suspends the municipal overweight, its paired four-point investment-grade corporate underweight is suspended and both return to neutral; this is not an ordinary-drift automatic rebalance and requires escalation for a Committee decision.

Managers may not directly adopt replacement research into a binding weight; the Committee may re-adopt a successor control only after an escalation record identifies the affected derived weights and accounts.

Revenue Procedure 2025-41 continues separate AMT-preference exceptions for specified residential-rental exempt-facility bonds, qualified mortgage bonds, qualified veterans’ mortgage bonds, and qualifying refunding bonds tied to pre-1986-08-08 obligations.

The allocation guide limits automatic suspension to a cited research note being superseded or withdrawn; a regulatory overlay that affects a research premise does not itself supply a suspension or replacement-weight rule.

SEC Order IA-7104, effective 2026-06-29, adjusts the Rule 205-3 qualified-client tests to at least $1,400,000 under management immediately after entering the advisory contract or a reasonable pre-contract belief that net worth exceeds $2,700,000.

The Private Markets Client Eligibility Determination Guide implements SEC Order IA-7104 Q.2 by requiring a qualified-client determination under either order test on or after its effective date and directing personnel to the order rather than restating its adjustable thresholds.

A pre-2026-06-29 qualified-client determination remains effective for the advisory contract or private-fund investment entered into before that date, but cannot support a new contract, subscription, or investment on or after it; the eligibility guide implements this by requiring prior-threshold identification and retesting a new subscription at adjusted amounts.

Order IA-7104 adjusts only Rule 205-3's qualified-client dollar tests; it leaves Regulation D accredited-investor criteria and the Investment Company Act section 2(a)(51) qualified-purchaser definition unchanged, and the eligibility guide implements that boundary by determining accredited-investor status separately.

An adviser relying on an Order IA-7104 determination must retain the Rule 204-2(a)(8) record of its basis, including the dollar test and date; the eligibility guide additionally records pathway, evidence, determiner, and date, treats an undocumented basis as no determination in audit, and marks carried-forward determinations as made under prior thresholds.

Private-markets eligibility must be determined and documented before an offer and is outside portfolio-manager discretion; a commitment also requires approval, but approval cannot clear an ineligible client, and separate suitability and liquidity requirements remain before commitment.

For the Rule 205-3 net-worth test, the primary residence value and indebtedness secured by it up to fair market value are excluded, while a natural person may include jointly held spousal assets; Order IA-7104 does not modify these calculation rules.

EQ-GL-AI-INFRA-POWER edition 2026-01 is a global view, published 2026-01-22 and applicable to positions taken on or after 2026-02-01; it overweights regulated utilities with data-centre load growth in their territories and electrical-equipment manufacturers with transformer and switchgear capacity, while holding no directional compute-vendor view.

The 2026-01 power view expects the binding constraint on AI infrastructure build-out to move from accelerator supply through 2024 to electrical infrastructure through 2026—specifically interconnection queue position, transformer lead times, and, in some jurisdictions, generation adequacy—and bases its investment case on economic rent moving with that constraint.

The note reports that median interconnection-study completion in the largest US market operator exceeds 40 months and says queue reform reduced speculative-project counts without materially shortening timelines for projects that remain.

For the highest-voltage classes, the power view puts large power-transformer lead times at three to four years and models capacity additions announced through 2025 as insufficient to close the gap before 2029.

EQ-GL-AI-INFRA-POWER 2026-01 P.4 modifies EQ-US-SEMI-CAPEX 2026-02 S.4 directionally: grid-interconnection timelines increasingly gate leading-edge fab siting, capping the rate of new capacity addition rather than the level of eventual demand.

The power thesis identifies material improvement in compute energy efficiency, regulatory allocation of interconnection capacity away from data-centre load, and a slowdown in AI capital formation as risks to its load-growth premise.

EQ-GL-AI-INFRA-POWER edition 2026-01 is an initiation with no prior view; it attributes the investment case to the movement of the binding AI-infrastructure constraint from accelerator supply through 2024 to electrical constraints through 2026, following the premise that economic rent moves with the constraint.

EQ-GL-AI-INFRA-POWER 2026-01 P.4 modifies EQ-US-SEMI-CAPEX 2026-02 S.4 only by treating grid interconnection as a cap on the rate of leading-edge capacity addition rather than eventual demand; the relationship supplies no different semiconductor weight or allocation instruction.

EQ-US-SEMI-CAPEX edition 2026-02, published 2026-02-19 and applicable to positions taken on or after 2026-03-01, positions US semiconductor capital equipment at neutral, reduced from overweight because of valuation and cycle position rather than deteriorating fundamentals.

EQ-US-SEMI-CAPEX 2026-02 S.1 supersedes EQ-US-SEMI-CAPEX 2025-06 S.1 for positions taken on or after 2026-03-01, while 2025-06 remains the basis of record for positions taken while it stood and for later review of those positions.
The 2025-06 edition was published on 2025-06-11, applied to positions taken from 2025-07-01, and held an overweight view on US semiconductor capital equipment over a 12-to-18-month horizon.

The 2025-06 overweight case rested on an early wafer-fab-equipment expansion, extending lithography and deposition lead times, and structurally improved customer concentration; it expressed the view through capital equipment and held no fabless or memory view.

The 2025-06 edition named reductions in either of the two largest logic customers' capex guidance, sustained below-cash-cost memory pricing, and materially restrictive export controls as conditions that would change its view.

The 2026-02 edition was published on 2026-02-19, applies to positions taken on or after 2026-03-01, and reduces US semiconductor capital equipment to neutral from overweight because the earlier cycle thesis largely played out on valuation and cycle position rather than deteriorating fundamentals.

In 2026-02, six consecutive quarters of wafer-fab-equipment spending growth and modestly shortening deposition lead times support a late-cycle reading; the desk treats the lead-time reversal as ordinary late-cycle behavior rather than a demand event.

The 2026-02 edition retains the customer-concentration structural argument, reporting a 46% top-three-customer share and stating that it is not the reason for the downgrade; it sets a neutral weight and prefers lithography over deposition and etch on pricing-power grounds.

A grid-interconnection constraint newly identified in 2026-02 increasingly gates leading-edge-fab siting and caps the rate of capacity addition rather than eventual demand; the global AI-infrastructure-power note defines it as a modifier to, not a replacement for, the semiconductor capital-equipment cycle view.

FI-US-DURATION-PATH Edition 2026-10, published 2026-10-06 and applicable to positions taken on or after 2026-11-01, recommends a modest +0.4-year duration position versus benchmark in the five-to-ten-year sector and excludes a long-end duration expression.

The duration view is a modest scenario deviation: the desk assumes one further policy-rate increase over 12 months versus 1.5 increases implied by the market, and states that this half-step difference is the whole recommendation rather than a conviction call.

In September 2026, the FOMC raised the target range by 25 basis points to 3-3/4 to 4 percent because it judged a somewhat more restrictive stance appropriate, while stating that inflation remained elevated relative to its 2 percent objective.

The view excludes a long-end duration expression because the desk sees term premium as fair to cheap, heavy long-end supply, and no catalyst for compression within 12 months; such a position would be a term-premium view the desk does not hold.

The stated risks are inflation prints that turn the desk's assumed single increase into a sequence, a fiscal event that increases long-end supply beyond projections, and a disorderly term-premium repricing that would hurt the front-loaded position; the note also cites three July dissents favoring an increase.

The FOMC continues balance-sheet reductions at the previously announced pace with no announced change, and says it will assess incoming data and the outlook at each meeting rather than commit to a sequence of future target-range adjustments.

The September FOMC statement expressly describes no future policy path: when considering additional adjustments it will weigh policy effects, lags, and economic and financial developments, and may adjust the stance if risks impede its goals. The desk's one-increase case is therefore its own scenario assumption rather than Federal Reserve guidance.
The desk expects continued 2s10s steepening and recommends a steepening bias rather than a parallel duration extension.

FI-US-IG-SPREADS edition 2025-09, published 2025-09-18 and applicable to positions on or after 2025-10-01, is underweight US investment-grade corporate credit because spreads are inside the tenth percentile of their 20-year range and provide limited compensation for cyclical risk.

The IG underweight is valuation-led rather than a credit-deterioration call: option-adjusted spreads are near their tightest levels since 2007 even after adjustments for improved average rating and shorter duration, while index leverage is stable and interest coverage comfortable.
The research note expresses the IG view as an approximately four-percentage-point taxable-fixed-income-sleeve underweight whose proceeds fund a higher-conviction sleeve position rather than cash.

The allocation guide, rather than the research note, creates the binding 28% investment-grade-corporate target versus 32% neutral and pairs its four-point underweight with the top-bracket municipal allocation's 22% target versus 18% neutral.

Under the allocation guide, suspension of the municipal overweight also suspends its paired IG-corporate underweight and returns both to neutral, preventing an unsupported structural short-credit position.

The desk identifies continued liability-driven demand, growth acceleration validating current spreads, and the carry cost of a prolonged range-bound market as the principal risks to the IG underweight.

A superseded or withdrawn cited research note suspends the derived allocation-guide weight and requires escalation to the Committee; a manager may neither carry the old weight forward nor directly adopt a replacement research recommendation.

The IG target has a ±2-percentage-point month-end market-value tolerance band, with ordinary drift rebalanced in the next monthly cycle, whereas a suspension-driven breach is not automatically rebalanced because the correct successor weight is a Committee decision.

For clients below the top federal marginal bracket, the US Taxable Account Fixed Income Allocation Guide sets municipal credit at its 18% neutral weight and does not apply the private-activity concentration.

FI-US-MUNI-CREDIT edition 2025-06, published 2025-06-12 and applicable to positions taken on or after 2025-07-01, recommends a two- to four-percentage-point taxable-fixed-income municipal overweight funded from investment-grade corporate credit and concentrated in high-yield and lower-investment-grade private-activity bonds.

The 2025-06 private-activity recommendation is load-bearingly an after-tax, top-federal-bracket view: a phase-out reduction that draws materially more holders into AMT means M.1 does not survive, while credit fundamentals alone support only neutral to modest overweight.

IRS Revenue Procedure 2025-41 N.3 supersedes FI-US-MUNI-CREDIT 2025-06 M.2 as to the threshold-dependent after-tax premise for affected taxpayers in taxable years beginning on or after 2026-01-01: it sets lower phase-out thresholds, reduces the AMT exemption above them, and applies the specified-PAB treatment to taxpayers above them regardless of prior thresholds, matching M.2's stated invalidation condition.

IRS Revenue Procedure 2025-41 N.5 preserves the qualified-501(c)(3) exception: its interest is not an AMT preference and the procedure's revised amounts do not apply to it; this instrument-level exception does not restore the M.2 rationale for non-excepted instruments or affected taxpayers.

For edition 2025-06, preferred PAB sectors are qualifying nonprofit hospitals, private higher education, and large-hub airport special-facility paper; the research expresses the overweight in 8–15 years and excludes extension beyond 15 years at current ratios.

The taxable fixed-income guide adopts FI-US-MUNI-CREDIT 2025-06 M.1/M.2 as a 22% versus 18% municipal target for top-bracket accounts, applies binding sector and duration limits, and pairs the four-point municipal overweight with a four-point investment-grade corporate underweight that returns to neutral when the municipal overweight is suspended.

FI-US-MUNI-CREDIT 2025-06 requires immediate review and re-issue after an announced change to the M.2 tax treatment; separately, when a cited note is superseded or withdrawn, allocation and discretion controls require escalation and prohibit mechanically rebalancing the suspension, carrying the prior weight forward, or directly adopting replacement research as a binding weight.
MA-GL-PRIVATE-MARKETS edition 2025-12 was published by Multi-Asset Research on 2025-12-10, takes a global view, and applies to positions taken on or after 2026-01-01.

For eligible clients with a genuine ten-year horizon, MA-GL-PRIVATE-MARKETS 2025-12 supports a 10–20% strategic private-markets allocation, weighted toward secondaries and private credit and away from primary buyout at current entry multiples.
The research note identifies secondaries as the most attractive private-markets entry point because discounts to NAV for buyout portfolios, though narrowed, remain wider than the ten-year median.
The research note regards private-credit spreads over broadly syndicated loans as adequate illiquidity compensation while monitoring deteriorating covenant quality at the larger end of the market.
The research note recommends underweighting rather than avoiding primary buyout because entry multiples are above its fair-value estimate and the exit environment has not normalised.

MA-GL-PRIVATE-MARKETS 2025-12 V.6 recommends underwriting private-markets exposure against client spending requirements rather than expected return and limiting unfunded commitments to two years of liquid-portfolio spending.
Global Multi-Asset Allocation Bands B.6 constrains implementation of the research liquidity recommendation by making the two-years-of-liquid-portfolio-spending cap on unfunded commitments binding.

Global Multi-Asset Allocation Bands B.2 and B.6 set a 10% private-markets sleeve for eligible global balanced clients and manage it through commitment pacing: denominator-effect drift is not traded, while over-commitment drift is a pacing failure subject to escalation.
MA-GL-PRIVATE-MARKETS 2025-12 treats qualified-client and accredited-investor eligibility as a regulatory constraint rather than a research conclusion, so its view applies only to eligible clients.

The Private Markets Eligibility Determination Guide constrains offers and commitments by requiring documented eligibility before an offer, and separately requiring suitability and the V.6 liquidity constraint before a commitment.

The private-markets note identifies prolonged exit-market closure and drawdown denominator effects as risks because the asset class cannot be rebalanced and allocation bands may be mechanically breached.

Eligibility, suitability, liquidity, and approval are separate private-markets controls: eligibility must be determined and documented before an offer and is outside portfolio-manager discretion; suitability and the liquidity constraint apply before commitment; every commitment requires approval, which cannot substitute for eligibility or clear a regulatory breach.
Edition 2026-02 of the global rates-regime research was published on 2026-02-05, applies to positions taken on or after 2026-03-01, and uses a global scope.
The note's working assumption is that real short rates move from persistently negative post-2010 levels to a 0% to 1.5% band through the cycle.

The note says higher real short rates reduce the equilibrium equity risk premium required for duration-like equities and make fixed income more attractive than in the post-2010 experience, supporting a higher strategic fixed-income weight than bands in force through 2023.

Because equity-duration correlation is unstable and has been positive for extended periods, the note recommends underwriting duration's diversification benefit at a materially lower level than the post-2010 sample implies rather than assuming reliably negative correlation will return.
The research recommends reviewing global multi-asset bands against its rate-regime and correlation conclusions, but explicitly does not set bands; setting them is a committee matter.

A demand-shock return to the post-2010 regime and fiscal dominance that deliberately holds nominal rates below inflation are stated as outcomes that invalidate the R.1 assumption, with opposite asset implications in the fiscal-dominance case.

The Investment Policy Committee adopted the reduced duration-diversification underwriting in March 2026, making it the basis for the 5-point equity band instead of the prior 7-point band; it accepted the note's R.1 working assumption for assessment at the 2026 annual review but has not changed strategic weights for it.

The committee's strategic default is 45% global equities, 35% global fixed income, 10% real assets, and 10% private markets for eligible clients, with ordinary ±5-point equity and fixed-income bands; these are committee controls rather than bands set by the research note.

A band resting on a research note is suspended if the note is superseded or withdrawn and returns to the prior committee-adopted level pending review; the guidance is reviewed annually and out of cycle when cited research is reissued or withdrawn.
MA-GL-RATES-REGIME 2026-02 is a framework note with no directional recommendation, so it is not itself a mandate-level trade or band instruction.

For clients not eligible for private markets, the committee guidance reallocates the 10% private-markets allocation pro rata across liquid sleeves; real assets have a ±3-point band and private markets have no ordinary tradable tolerance band.

When a mandate guide cites research that is superseded or withdrawn, the portfolio manager must escalate rather than re-derive or carry forward the derived weight; only the Committee may adopt a replacement binding control.
